results.title: Inclusive AI-Enhanced Civic Engagement: Empowering ... - MDPI
results.content: Consequently, the first research question addressed in study 1 is: (1) “Which platform features and AI-enabled supports do citizens from vulnerable groups prefer and perceive as helpful for overcoming participation barriers?”. To address our first research questions, we recruited citizens from vulnerable groups in two European cities with low rankings in digital skills and infrastructure (DESI) [10] to co-design an inclusive online civic engagement platform and surveyed the citizens regarding technical preferences and wishes in the first study. Features were compiled from a review of commonly implemented civic-participation platform functions, as well as prior work on digital exclusion mechanisms affecting vulnerable groups (e.g., language barriers, literacy and comprehension barriers, accessibility needs, safety/trust concerns, and navigation challenges). Unlike prior technology design research that either excluded citizens from vulnerable groups from participatory design [33] or focused primarily on the technical dimensions of AI transparency e.g., [34], our work foregrounds the role of user education about AI features and thus addresses an underexplored pathway to equitable technology adoption.

results.title: AI for Public Good: Advancing Inclusive, Data-Driven, and Future ...
results.content: Within the context of public governance, AI offers governments powerful tools to improve decision-making, increase service efficiency, and enable data-driven social policy. These examples show that when AI is embedded strategically, not merely as a technology investment but as a governance enabler, it generates cumulative public value, enhances institutional agility, and contributes to broader social outcomes such as equity, well-being, and sustainable economic growth. By prioritizing AI for urban sustainability, citizen services, and public infrastructure, regional leaders like Saudi Arabia and the UAE are establishing themselves as testbeds for next-generation digital governance. By embedding AI into the infrastructure of public services, environmental protection, and economic opportunity creation, regional governments position themselves as champions of inclusive, human-centered innovation; demonstrating how technology can tangibly improve everyday life. As governments increasingly harness AI to improve public services, equity, and well-being, several challenges must be addressed to ensure that the benefits of AI are broadly shared, ethically managed, and strategically aligned with national development goals.
